- When sentiment is consistently low (≤0.4) over recent days, model tends to overestimate prices; reduce forecast by 5–10% in next 7–14 days.
- After a sharp price spike (forecast > +10% above recent mean), model often overshoots; cap forecast at +5% above peak or adjust downward by 3–5 points if sentiment drops.
- If sentiment is high (≥0.7) and price is falling, model often fails to recognize mean reversion; add 1–2 points of downward correction if sentiment >0.6 and price >+5% above 30d mean.
- Model underestimates when sentiment is volatile (alternating 0.3–0.7) — increase forecast by 2–4% if sentiment swings >0.2 in last 5 days.
- For 30-day horizon, if true outcome is below 70% of 30d moving average, model often misses the drop — apply a 3–5 point downward bias if sentiment <0.4 and price >75.
- If sentiment is high but price is falling, model often overcorrects — reduce forecast by 1–3 points if sentiment >0.7 and price <75.
- When sentiment is low and price is rising, model often fails to recognize momentum — increase forecast by 1–3 points if sentiment <0.4 and price >80.
